speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to understand the specific characteristics of your skin lesions to evaluate any potential oncologic implications. Can you describe the appearance, size, and how quickly they have changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of heavy smoking and a non-healing, crusty lesion on your penis and finger is concerning; could you tell me if any of these lesions have bled, ulcerated, or have irregular borders?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma

The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures are consistent with malignancy rather than pneumonia. Given the heavy smoking history and the location of the lesions, I suspect Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Do you have any history of chronic ulcers, burns, or other trauma to these specific areas?
